Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Pinnacle Power Holdings Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Director of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Pinnacle Power Holdings' Q3 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Torres, Chief Operating Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Strategy Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Regulatory Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by the accelerated retirement of our fossil fuel plants and our replacement strategies, meaningful progress on grid modernization and smart grid initiatives, strong advancement on our strategic initiatives and long-term goals, a favorable revenue breakdown across our regulated and unregulated segments, effective storm response and recovery efforts, an overview of financial performance that exceeded our guidance, and a promising rate base growth outlook with solid key assumptions.

Let me provide some more detail on these key aspects, starting with our progress on strategic initiatives and long-term goals. As we wrap up our Q3 results, we're making measurable headway across our three core pillars: accelerating the clean energy transition, modernizing our grid for reliability and resilience, and driving sustainable growth through disciplined capital allocation. This positions Pinnacle to deliver superior total shareholder returns while meeting customers' evolving needs in a decarbonizing world.

Our clean energy transition remains central to our vision of 80% carbon-free generation by 2035 and net-zero Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2045, ahead of many peers. In Q3, we brought online 850 MW of new renewables, including the 450 MW Wind Ridge project in the Texas Panhandle and 400 MW of utility-scale solar in the Southeast with First Solar's Series 7 modules. Year-to-date renewables additions total 2.1 GW, 15% ahead of our 1.8 GW full-year guidance. Our renewables portfolio now at 12.4 GW makes up 42% of our 29.5 GW regulated and contracted fleet, up 500 basis points year-over-year. Wind capacity factors hit 38%, aided by GE Vernova's 5.X turbine controls, while solar averages 26% DC capacity factor, supported by IRA ITC transferability unlocking $1.2 billion in monetized credits year-to-date. We've secured 1.8 GW of new PPAs at $42/MWh average, a 12% premium to LevelTen benchmarks, with most extending 15+ years and CPI escalators.

Our 15 GW renewables pipeline, valued at over $25 billion, is 60% permitted, with shovel-ready projects in PJM and SPP. We're on pace for 2.5 GW additions in 2025 via 50/50 regulated and contracted funding at 10.2% ATRR. On fossil optimization, we retired 1.2 GW of coal this year, including the 600 MW Black Mesa plant, dropping coal to under 8% of our mix. Backfills include 900 MW CCGT peakers from Mitsubishi Power. Our 1.8 GW nuclear fleet ran at 93.5% capacity factor in Q3, and we're piloting SMRs with NuScale by 2029 in Idaho.

Grid modernization investments totaled $450 million year-to-date, like the 345 kV Summit-to-Hub line in CAISO unlocking 1.2 GW renewables and cutting SAIDI 18% to 65 minutes. AMI covers 85% of our 2.5 million customers, curbing peak demand 12% in pilots and deferring $800 million T&D capex. Battery storage hit 1.2 GW with Q3's 450 MW/1,050 MWh Falcon project in ERCOT, earning $150/kW-year in ancillaries at 14% IRRs and aggregating 500 MW in VPPs.

Regionally, Southeast load grew 4.5% on data center PPAs totaling 800 MW at $65/MWh. Midwest MISO auctions cleared $12/kW-month for 3,000 MW. California wildfire capex rose 20% to $250 million but earns 10.5% ROE. Electrification efforts include 5,000 Level 2 chargers and 200 MW demand response. Financially, 2024 capex guidance is $4.8 billion, up 10%, with 65% to renewables/storage at 6.2% AFUDC, driving 6-8% EPS CAGR, 95% FCF conversion, and a 4.5% dividend hike to $2.48/share. Long-term: 50 GW capacity by 2030 (60% carbon-free), $7 billion EBITDA, 7-9% EPS growth on $50 billion 10-year capex.

Sarah, over to you to expand on the retirement of fossil fuel plants, grid modernization, revenue breakdown, storm response, financial performance versus guidance, and rate base outlook.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning, everyone. Let's start with the accelerated retirement of our legacy fossil fuel plants and comprehensive replacement strategies, central to net-zero by 2045 while ensuring reliability, affordability, and shareholder returns.

Over the past decade, sector shifts from EPA Clean Air Act rules, 45% average RPS targets in our 12-state footprint, solar LCOE at $24-32/MWh per Lazard 2023, and IRA incentives like 30-50% ITCs and 45V hydrogen PTC make this economic. Our 45-year-old coal fleet's O&M exceeds $35/MWh amid gas volatility.

In Q3, we retired 1,200 MW coal at our Mid-Atlantic PJM facility, 8% of fossil fleet, per our 2023-2025 plan for 2,800 MW more. Year-to-date cuts Scope 1 emissions 15% or 4.2 million metric tons CO2e, 20% ahead of SBTi targets. Saved $180 million in costs versus $45 million decommissioning, below $50-60 million/500 MW guidance via asset sales.

Replacements: 1,500 MW online year-to-date, 1:1 swap with 99.98% SAIDI/SAIFI. Renewables include ERCOT's 450 MW Lone Star Solar+Storage with Trina modules and Tesla Megapacks at $28/MWh LCOE, capturing $5,000/MWh peaks and $120 million BRA proceeds. Southeast's 800 MW Atlantic Wind Phase 1 (300 MW) uses Siemens Gamesa 14 MW turbines at 40% ITC. Storage: 1.2 GW/4.8 GWh, including 100 MW/400 MWh iron-air with Form Energy at $220/kWh, 85% efficiency for duck curve. CCGTs: 600 MW in MISO at 64% heat rates, hydrogen-ready. 2023 replacement capex $2.1 billion at 6.8% after-tax cost, 60% green bonds.

Regionally: PJM RPE for solar reconductoring; CAISO VPPs defer $100 million T&D; ERCOT merchant at $85/MWh. De-risks fuel to 8% EBITDA; 70% zero-carbon fleet; $300 million ITC sales. Customer DERMS enroll 2 million, shaving 1.2 GW peaks. 2024-2028 IRP: 5 GW renewables, 2 GW storage, 1.5 GW gas, retiring 4 GW fossil for 6-8% EPS CAGR.

Next, grid modernization and smart grid initiatives, key amid 25% renewables penetration and 15 GW EV load by 2030. $1.2 billion capex over three years (18% of spend) cut SAIDI 22% to 85 minutes, SAIFI 19% to 0.95, saving $45 million O&M and hitting J.D. Power 785/1000.

AMI at 95% of 2.8 million meters integrates with Oracle NMS; Q3 demand response shaved 450 MW, avoiding $12 million PJM buys. ADMS from GE GridOS optimizes volt/VAR, cutting losses 8% or 120 GWh ($15 million saved). DERMS manages 5,000 assets, handling 250 MW rooftop PV per FERC 2222.

Regional: Northeast $450 million microgrids cut polar vortex impacts; South 5G PMUs boost capacity 12%; Midwest EV pilots for $30 million revenues. Grid edge services $18 million Q3 recurring; NIST cybersecurity; Scope 2 cuts 11%. 2024 $450 million Phase 2: AI analytics for 20% SAIDI drop, $60 million GaaS.

Now, revenue breakdown: Q3 consolidated $3.2 billion, up 8% YoY. Regulated 68% or $2.18 billion, up 12%; YTD $6.5 billion. $1.2 billion rate base growth at 10.2% ROE; Indiana $450 million settlement recovers $800 million storage/grid; Southeast 6% volumes, $150 million weather uplift; Q4 $600 million filing for $2.5 billion capex; $45 million AFUDC.

Unregulated 32% or $1.02 billion, up 15%; YTD $2.9 billion, 28% EBITDA margins. 15 GW fleet: PJM $28/MWh spreads, $270/MW-day auctions; ERCOT 95% gas factors $350 million; nuclear uprate; 5 TWh renewables trading; $180 million retail. Hy Stor JV for H2. FY24 unregulated EBITDA $1.1-1.2 billion.

Storm response for Hurricane Zeta: Category 3 hit Southeast with 120 mph winds, 15 inches rain; 1.47 million outages (28%), 4,200 miles down. Mobilized 4,000 personnel via EEI; critical restored in 12 hours, 65% by 48, 98% by day 5; SAIDI 145 minutes vs. 210 average.

Drones/LiDAR, AMI, mobile SCADA, microgrids aided. Costs $285 million ($0.18 EPS hit), offset by $95 million insurance/$65 million riders; net $0.10 FY drag, recoverable at 10.5% ROE. Florida 850k outages, 72-hour avg; Georgia 50 hours; Carolinas lighter. $2.8 billion Resilience Program: 35% undergrounding, smart reclosers, DERMS 1.2 GW, AI vegetation.

Financial performance vs. guidance: Revenues $2.72 billion beat $2.55 billion midpoint 6.7%, up 8% YoY; C&I 15.2 million MWh on data centers. EPS $1.42 beat $1.20-1.30; EBITDA $885 million beat $800-850 million at 32.5% margins; fuel $28/MWh.

Regulated EBITDA $485 million top of guide, rate base $18.5 billion; Competitive $320 million beat on $52/MWh prices, ERCOT gas/renewables; Corporate $80 million. Generation 28.6 million MWh; capex $625 million. Raised FY24 EBITDA $3.45-3.55 billion, EPS $5.25-5.45; 2025 7-9% growth.

Rate base outlook: $28.4 billion now; 6.0-6.5% CAGR to $37.5 billion by 2028. Capex $2.8-3.4 billion: 45% T&D ($1.3 billion resiliency/undergrounding); 30% renewables/storage (800 MW solar, 400 MW BESS); 25% AMI/DER. Assumptions: 90% CWIP, 9-10 months lag, 9.75-10.25% ROE; 1.2-1.5% load growth (EVs/data centers); 2.5% inflation, $400 million equity. Southeast 7% CAGR, Midwest 4.5%.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Torres to discuss operations.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. For Q3, we reported earnings per share of $1.42 and revenue of $2.72 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $625 million, primarily focused on renewables and grid modernization. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders. We anticipate 7-9% EPS growth in 2025.

Michael Torres: Thank you, Sarah. Let me provide an update on the operational front. We are seeing improved efficiency in our combined-cycle gas turbine power plants due to the implementation of advanced turbine controls. This has resulted in a 10% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 15%.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Michael. Turning to our long-term strategy, we are actively exploring opportunities in the battery storage space. We believe this will be a key driver of future growth. We are also evaluating potential acquisitions in the Southeast US market.

Dr. Raj Patel: Thank you, Elena. From a technology perspective, we are making significant investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity. We recently deployed an AI-driven threat detection system to enhance our defenses against cyber threats. We are also piloting advanced metering infrastructure in our California service territory.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Dr. Patel. On the regulatory front, we received approval for our rate case settlement in PJM and MISO. This will allow us to recover $450 million in investments.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Sarah, Michael, Elena, Dr. Raj, and Lisa. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for renewable expansion?

Johnathan Hale: Certainly. Our renewables pipeline stands at 15 GW, with 2.5 GW targeted for 2025, blending regulated and contracted structures. We've already exceeded YTD guidance with 2.1 GW added, securing premium PPAs and leveraging IRA credits for strong returns.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: What is your outlook for capex?

Sarah Jenkins: Our 2024 capex is $4.8 billion, with 65% to renewables and storage. Looking to 2025-2028, we see steady ramp to $3.4 billion annually, focused on rate base-accretive projects at 6.2% AFUDC, supporting 6-8% EPS growth while maintaining leverage.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee: How are you mitigating risks related to supply chain?

Michael Torres: We're hedging forward with domestic sourcing under IRA 45X credits, maintaining a 3 GW inventory buffer. Lessons from delays on panels and transformers have us prioritizing U.S. fabrication, minimizing impacts as seen in our on-schedule solar and storage deployments.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Patel: What is the anticipated impact of the regulatory environment on your earnings?

Lisa Chen: Approvals like our recent rate settlements enable full recovery of $450 million plus ongoing formula rates at 10.2% ROE. We're advocating for FERC incentives and state riders, de-risking capex and supporting our 6-8% CAGR outlook with minimal lag.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in Q3, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Pinnacle Power Holdings for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Pinnacle Power Holdings.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
